metas.name: Agriculture - Hop
metas.note: Hop fields are mainly found between Ingolstadt and Landshut - an area called 'Hallertau/Holledau' in Bavaria. There are some minor regions in Thuringia, Saxony-Anhalt and Saxony as well.

metas.name: Agriculture - Vineyards
metas.note: There are 13 wine regions in Germany. They are mostly concentrated in the southwest of Germany. However, there are a couple regions further east as well, along the border between Thuringia and Saxony-Anhalt, as well as along the Elbe in Saxony.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt, Deutsches Weininstitut

metas.name: Architecture - Arches in Half-Timbered houses
metas.note: This type of half-timbered house with arches at the ground floor is very common in this region of Saxony.

metas.name: Architecture - Commie Blocks
metas.note: These large, utilitarian apartment buildings constructed during the socialist era, that are also known as 'Commie blocks' are common in all of former East Germany.

metas.name: Architecture - Fishscale Walls
metas.note: Houses with black slate walls, resembling fish scales, are commonly found in a large area of central Germany.

metas.name: Architecture - Frisian Architecture
metas.note: Thatched roofs and rock walls are most common on the North Frisian Islands, as well as mainland Schleswig-Holstein. You can also commonly find them in coastal resort towns in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.

metas.name: Architecture - Red Brick
metas.note:
These brick houses are generally concentrated in northwestern Germany.

NOTE: This map is very approximate.

metas.name: Camera Meta - Low Cam
metas.note: Lowcam coverage can be found around Singen and near Switzerland.

metas.name: Car Meta - Gen 3 / Antenna
metas.note: This rare Generation 3 car coverage with an antenna can be found in central Hamburg (Speicherstadt). Note by MB: This is officially a trekker, so you won't find any copyright.

metas.name: Car Meta - Gen 3 Black Car
metas.note:
You can find a Generation 3 black car in this safari park southeast of Bielefeld.

You can commonly see 4x4s painted with a zebra pattern in the park.

NOTE: This car is unique to this park within all of Europe.

metas.name: Car Meta - White/Black Gen 4 Car
metas.note:
You can find this rare white and black Generation 4 car in Hamburg and around Frankfurt.

NOTE: You can also find the same car around London and in Ireland.

metas.name: Infrastructure - ALDI Nord
metas.note: There are two regional Aldi chains, which have split Germany in two; Aldi Süd in the south, and Aldi Nord in the north.

metas.name: Infrastructure - ALDI Süd
metas.note: There are two regional Aldi chains, which have split Germany in two; Aldi Süd in the south, and Aldi Nord in the north.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Black Disk Bollard
metas.note: Bollards standing on these black disks are commonly found in all of eastern Germany.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bus Stop - Berlin
metas.note: Berlin uses segmented bus stops, with a yellow signpost.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bus Stop - Bremen
metas.note: Bremen proper uses simple bus stops, which have the bus stop name within a red section. The edges can be rounded.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bus Stop - Bremerhaven
metas.note: Bremerhaven, which is still part of Bremen, uses bus stops with a grey section on the opposite side of the signpost. And the bus stop name is red within a yellow section.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bus Stop - Hamburg
metas.note: Hamburg bus stops have a red signpost, and the route numbers are within hexagons. Note that they can be found outside of Hamburg as well

metas.name: Infrastructure - Capped Bollard
metas.note: Some bollards in North Rhine-Westphalia have a green bit at the top. The top can also be another colour.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Cologne Lamppost Plate
metas.note:
Lampposts in Cologne will often feature these bright yellow numbers on a black piece of plastic.

NOTE: Similar looking things can be found elsewhere as well.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Curved Poletop
metas.note: Pole tops which have a curved horizontal bar can be found in Bavaria, though they are rare.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Dark Reflector
metas.note: Bollards with darker reflectors than usual are commonly found in Schleswig-Holstein, Niedersachsen, Nordrhein-Westfalen, Bavaria. They can sometimes be found in Baden-Württemberg and rarely in Hesse.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Grey Bollard Plate
metas.note: Baden-Württemberg is the only state where the plates on the bollards can be grey instead of white.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Lower Half Missing Bollard
metas.note: These irregular looking bollards, which do not have a white encasing on the bottom half, are found on K-roads in this region of Lower Saxony, around Lüneburg. K-Roads in this region will not have any other type of bollard.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Lower Saxony km Marker
metas.note: You can find these simple rectangular markers, with rounded edges in Lower Saxony.

metas.name: Infrastructure - LVR Cap
metas.note: Some of the green caps will have the text ‘LVR’, along with a small coat of arms. These specific green caps are unique to southern North Rhine-Westphalia.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Metal Border km Marker - Lower Saxony
metas.note: These markers with a metallic border around the marker itself are found in Schleswig-Holstein and Lower Saxony. The numbers after the comma are usually smaller on the markers in Lower Saxony.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Metal Border km Marker - Schleswig-Holstein
metas.note: These markers with a metallic border around the marker itself are found in Schleswig-Holstein and Lower Saxony. The numbers after the comma are usually smaller on the markers in Lower Saxony (So if that's not the case go SchleHo)

metas.name: Infrastructure - Orange Bollard Plate
metas.note: Rhineland-Palatinate is the only state where the plates on the bollards are orange instead of white.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Orange Posts
metas.note: These simple orange posts are most commonly found in Bavaria, and also in the other highlighted states.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Red Cap Bollard
metas.note: These white posts with a red cap are found in all of former East Germany, but most commonly in the state of Saxony-Anhalt.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Round Concrete Poles
metas.note: These round concrete poles are almost unique to Former Eastern Germany.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Berlin
metas.note: Berlin uses white signs with a grey border, and a separate section for numbers under the street name. Also note how the letter ß looks.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Darmstadt
metas.note: Streetsigns in Darmstadt are white and often are written in ALL CAPS, which is unique in Germany.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Dortmund
metas.note: Dortmund uses blue signs with a white border and a grey frame. The signs also have a separate section for numbers under the street name.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Dresden
metas.note: Dresden has blue signs with a unique font.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Düsseldorf
metas.note: Düsseldorf has black signs with a white border, similar to Munich. The signs have a metallic frame.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Essen
metas.note: Essen has blue signs with a very thick metallic frame.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Frankfurt
metas.note: Frankfurt uses blue street signs with a metallic border around the sign, as well as the separate section for numbers under the street name.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Hanover
metas.note: Hanover uses white signs with a wider than usual gap between the sign and metallic frame.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Mainz
metas.note: Mainz has a mix of blue signs, and this unique red variant.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Munich
metas.note: Munich has blue street signs with a white decorative border that does not touch the corners. Also note the unique font.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Nuremberg
metas.note: Nuremberg has blue signs with a unique font. The signs also have a grey frame with a small gap between it and the sign.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Stuttgart
metas.note: Stuttgart uses black signs without a border.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Wuppertal
metas.note: Wuppertal uses white signs with a unique font and a white painted frame with a small gap between it and the sign.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Thicc T Pole
metas.note: These pole tops where the middle of the horizontal bar is thicker can be found in all of former East Germany.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Three Section Road Marker
metas.note: Bavaria uses these white rectangular road markers, which are divided by black lines into three sections. The left section provides the road you are currently on.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Trashcan - Berlin
metas.note: Berlin uses bright orange bins that have white text on them.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Trashcan - Bremen
metas.note: Bremen has green and grey bins, with orange speech bubbles.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Trashcan - Hamburg
metas.note: Hamburg uses bright red bins, with white speech bubbles.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Tree Tag
metas.note: Many trees in Brandenburg and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern have these tiny green markers on them. You can very rarely find them in Lower Saxony.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Triangle Poletop
metas.note: Triangle pole tops are common in Western Germany.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Triangle Post - Grey
metas.note: Baden-Württemberg uses grey triangle posts.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Triangle Post - North Rhine-Westphalia
metas.note: North Rhine-Westphalia uses white posts without white plates on the sides. You can also find posts which go all the way to the ground.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Triangle Post - Thuringia
metas.note: The plates on the Thuringia Triangle Posts are unique, as they have sections which are seperated by a black line.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Triangle Post - Unpainted
metas.note: Rhineland-Palatinate and Saxony use unpainted, rocky looking posts, with white plates stuck on each side.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Triangle Post - White
metas.note: Saarland, Thuringia, and Baden-Württemberg use white posts, with the same white plates attached. Note by MB: PlonkIt says they're smaller in BaWü. From what I saw, this is fake though.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Trident Poles
metas.note: These trident-like pole tops can be found in Bavaria, Saxony-Anhalt, and Baden-Württemberg.

metas.name: Infrastructure - White Bollard Plate
metas.note: These basic white plates on bollards can be found in all states except for Bavaria, Saarland and the City States.

metas.name: Infrastructure - White Tree Paint
metas.note:
You can spot trees that are painted white close to the bottom of the trunk in the northeast.

NOTE: You will rarely find them outside the shaded region.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Wooden Bollard
metas.note: These round wooden bollards, which have a painted top, are found in Bavaria.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Yellow Bollard - No Plate
metas.note: Fully yellow posts are found in the state of Brandenburg.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Yellow Bollard - Plate
metas.note:
Yellow posts with a white plate on them are found in Saxony-Anhalt.

NOTE: Sometimes there is only 1 plate, which can make it hard to tell apart from a Brandenburg post.

metas.name: Infrasturcture - Double Connector Signback
metas.note: The double connector signback is very common in Schleswig-Holstein and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. It is also found in Brandenburg. Rarely, you may see it in Saxony, Rhineland-Palatinate or Hamburg.

metas.name: Infrasturcture - Folded Sign
metas.note: Folded Signs are most common in Bremen, then Saxony-Anhalt and Saarland.

metas.name: Infrasturcture - No-Fold Signback
metas.note: Non-folded signbacks are most common in Schleswig-Holstein, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Hesse, Hamburg, Bremen, then Brandenburg, Saxony, Baden-Württemberg.

metas.name: Infrasturcture - Red Bicycle Sign
metas.note: Red bicycle signs can be found in Northrhine-Westphalia, Southern Lower Saxony and Hamburg.

metas.name: Infrasturcture - Saarland Bicycle Sign
metas.note: These dark-green designs can be found in Saarland only.

metas.name: Infrasturcture - Schleswig-Holstein Bicycle Sign
metas.note: Schleswig-Holstein sometimes uses slightly different cycling sign designs. For the one with town-names, note the difference in the arrow. For the one without, the shape is different.

metas.name: Infrasturcture - T-Signback
metas.note: The T-Signback is exclusive to Hamburg.

metas.name: Infrasturcture - Type A Guardrail
metas.note: I'd avise to learn where this cannot be found, which is Easter Germany, Hesse, Baden-Württemberg and Saarland.

metas.name: Infrasturcture - Type B Guardrail
metas.note: I'd avise to learn where this cannot be found, which is Schleswig-Holstein, Rhineland-Palatinate, Bremen and Hamburg.

metas.name: Landscape - Alps
metas.note: The German Alps is the most mountainous region in Germany, it is mostly concentrated on the Austrian Border.

metas.name: Landscape - Flat Landscape
metas.note: The North and especially Northwest of Germany is very flat.

metas.name: Landscape - Hilliness
metas.note: Central Germany is hilly.

metas.name: Landscape - Regensburg Plains & Ridge
metas.note: The flat plains southeast of Regensburg can be recognised by the slight ridge often visible to the northeast. The plains themselves are flat, and quite agricultural.

metas.name: Landscape - Sylt
metas.note:
The shrub and sand covered hills are unique to the island of Sylt. And like the rest of the North Frisian Islands, rock walls, brick houses, and thatched roofs are common.

NOTE: Some parts of Sylt look more generic, but still very flat.

metas.name: Language - Sorbian
metas.note: Sorbian, a Slavic language, is spoken near the Polish and Czech border. You can find it on a variety of signs in this region between Cottbus and Bautzen.

metas.name: Language - Town Suffix: -a
metas.note: The suffix -a can be found in the Southern Half of Germany.

metas.name: Language - Town Suffix: -ach
metas.note: The suffix -ach can be found in the Southern Half of Germany.

metas.name: Language - Town Suffix: -itz
metas.note: The suffix -itz can be found in Eastern Germany.

metas.name: Language - Town Suffix: -itzsch
metas.note: The suffix -itzsch can be found in Eastern Germany.

metas.name: Language - Town Suffix: -ow
metas.note: The suffix -ow can be found in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Berlin and Brandenburg.

metas.name: Language - Town Suffix: -schütz
metas.note: The suffix -schütz can be found in Eastern Germany.

metas.name: Language - Town Suffix: -weier
metas.note: The suffix -weiler can mainly be found in Rhineland-Palatinate, Saarland and Baden-Württemberg.

metas.name: Language - Town Suffix: -weiler
metas.note: The suffix -weiler can mainly be found in Rhineland-Palatinate, Saarland and Baden-Württemberg.

metas.name: Vegetation - Baltic Pines
metas.note: Baltic Pines or Pinus sylvestris are generally more concentrated in the northeast of Germany. They can be recognized by their orange-tinged trunk.
